en.name: Dried lily flower (golden needles)
en.summary: Dried daylily buds keep about 6–12 months in an airtight jar in a dark cupboard, and 12–18 months sealed in the fridge once the bag is open. Those figures are the general ones for dried vegetables as a class — no authority publishes a separate shelf life for golden needles.
en.pantry: Airtight and dark is the whole instruction: 6–12 months in a sealed jar in a cool, dry, dark cupboard. Read that range for what it is — it comes from guidance on dried vegetables in general, where one source gives roughly half a year in a cool room and another a full year at ordinary room temperature, so the honest answer spans both rather than sitting on a single number. Light is the enemy of colour here; a jar left on an open shelf bleaches from amber to pale straw. Warmth shortens the range at the same time, so keep the jar away from the hob and the window.
en.fridge: In a humid kitchen the fridge is the better cupboard: sealed tight, dried lily flower keeps 12–18 months at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. Squeeze the air out of the bag or use a jar with a gasket, because the buds pick up fridge smells readily and any moisture they absorb will let mould start. Soak them in cold water and rinse well before cooking, and treat the soaked buds as a fresh vegetable — refrigerate them and use them the same day.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for dried lily flower, and freezing a properly dried product gains little: the buds are already stable for months, and what threatens them is damp rather than time. If you do freeze a bulk purchase, seal it hard and let the pack come back to room temperature before opening it, or condensation will settle on the buds and undo the drying.
spoilage: Musty or mouldy smell, or visible fuzzy spots on the buds.
Buds that feel soft, damp or bendy instead of brittle and dry.
Clumping into a solid mass inside the bag.
Insect activity — small holes, webbing or grubs in the jar.
tips: Store in dark glass or an opaque jar; light bleaches the colour out.
A very bright, uniform yellow usually means sulphur dioxide treatment — soak and rinse thoroughly.
Soak in cold water rather than hot; hot water turns the buds mushy.
Buy small quantities often rather than a whole year's worth at once.

faq.q: How long do dried golden needles keep?
faq.a: About 6–12 months airtight in a dark cupboard, or 12–18 months sealed in the fridge. Those are the general figures for dried vegetables, not a daylily-specific published shelf life.

faq.q: Do dried lily flowers need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: Not necessarily, but in a humid climate the fridge roughly doubles the useful life. Seal the bag tightly first.

faq.q: Why are some golden needles so bright yellow?
faq.a: Usually sulphite treatment. Soak them in cold water and rinse thoroughly before cooking, and choose duller amber ones if you would rather avoid it.

zh.name: 乾金針
zh.summary: 乾金針密封避光放櫥櫃約可放 6～12 個月，開封後密封冷藏則是 12～18 個月。要提醒的是，這組數字來自「乾燥蔬菜」這一大類的通則，並沒有哪個單位為金針單獨發表過保存期限。
zh.pantry: 重點就四個字：密封、避光。密封罐放陰涼乾燥的暗處，約 6～12 個月。這個範圍該怎麼讀也要說清楚：它來自乾燥蔬菜的一般性建議，其中一份資料給的是涼爽室溫下大約半年，另一份給的是一般室溫下整整一年，所以誠實的答案是把兩者都涵蓋進來，而不是硬挑一個數字。這裡光線是顏色的頭號敵人，放在開放層架上的罐子會從琥珀色褪成稻草色；溫度偏高則會同時縮短上面那個範圍，所以罐子請遠離爐台和窗邊。
zh.fridge: 在潮濕的廚房，冰箱才是更好的櫥櫃：密封好放 4 °C 以下，乾金針可放 12～18 個月。袋子要把空氣擠掉，或用有膠條的密封罐，因為金針很會吸冰箱的味道，而只要吸到水氣就會開始長霉。烹調前用冷水泡開並確實沖洗乾淨；泡發後的金針要當成新鮮蔬菜看待，冷藏並且當天用完。
zh.freezer: 乾金針沒有公布的冷凍期限，而且把已經乾透的東西冷凍，好處有限：它本來就能穩定放上好幾個月，威脅它的是濕氣而不是時間。真的要冷凍一大包，請密封確實，並且要等整包回到室溫再打開，否則水氣會凝在金針上，把當初的乾燥全部白費。
spoilage: 有霉味或土味，或看得到絨毛狀霉斑。
金針摸起來軟、潮、可以折彎，而不是脆而乾。
有蟲，出現小孔、絲網或蟲體。
tips: 用深色玻璃罐或不透光容器，光線會把顏色漂掉。
顏色特別鮮黃又均勻的，通常是二氧化硫處理過的，泡洗要更確實。
用冷水泡，不要用熱水，熱水會泡爛。
少量多次買，不要一次囤一整年的量。

faq.a: 密封避光放櫥櫃約 6～12 個月，密封冷藏約 12～18 個月。這是乾燥蔬菜的通則數字，不是金針專屬的公布期限。
不一定，但在潮濕的氣候下，冷藏大約能把可用期限拉長一倍。前提是袋子要先密封好。

faq.q: 為什麼有些金針特別黃？
faq.a: 通常是經過亞硫酸鹽處理。烹調前用冷水泡開並徹底沖洗；不想碰的話，挑顏色偏暗琥珀色的。
